# Documents and layout steps

[Get
started](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/articles/v01-get-started.md)
built a document with one *layout step*: a step that takes the outputs
of other steps and arranges them with
[`pub_doc()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md) and
[`pub_section()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md).
This vignette is about what comes with real reports: inputs that fail,
reports that show only some of the steps, a number of sections that
depends on the data, a report over several pipelines, and how to test
all of this. It builds on pipeflow’s vignettes [Pipeline
views](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pipeflow/vignettes/v03b-pipeline-views.html),
[Error
handling](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pipeflow/vignettes/v05c-error-handling.html)
and [Split, map and
reduce](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pipeflow/vignettes/v05a-split-map-reduce.html).

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`pipeflow`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/)`)`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`pubflow`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/)`)`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org)`)`

### The example

The pipeline of Get started again: `airquality` data, a linear model of
the ozone concentration and a table, a figure and a text made from the
model. The figure is made by a function defined outside the pipeline,
which matters for [the last section](#steps-that-make-figures).

\

`coef_table` is a function defined outside the pipeline and given to
[`pip_add()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)
as it is. A function can’t say `~fit` in its own signature, so `params`
connects its argument `model` to the step `fit`. The step `plot` shows
the other way: an inline function that only calls the outside one.

### Failures in a document

If a step fails, the steps that depend on it can’t run. A report should
still show what is there, and say what is missing. That is the job of
`~try(step)` in a layout step: instead of skipping the layout step,
pipeflow hands it the *failure* of the input, and pubflow places it in
the document as an error box.

\
`pip`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(`\
`        ``"report"``,`\
`        ``function``(`\
`            ``table`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``data_table``)``,`\
`            ``coefs`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``coef_table``)``,`\
`            ``plot`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``plot``)``,`\
`            ``summary`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``summary``)`\
`        ``)`` ``{`\
`            `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(`\
`                `[`pub_section`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``"Data"``, ``table``)``,`\
`                `[`pub_section`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``"Results"``, ``summary``, ``coefs``, ``plot``)``,`\
`                title ``=`` ``"Ozone in New York"`\
`            ``)`\
`        ``}`\
`    ``)`

Make `fit` fail by asking for a variable that the data doesn’t have.
With `on_error = "continue"` the run goes on with the steps that don’t
depend on `fit`:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Height"``)``)`\
[`tryCatch`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/conditions.html)`(`\
`    `[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, on_error ``=`` ``"continue"``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)``,`\
`    warning ``=`` ``function``(``w``)`` `[`cat`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/cat.html)`(`[`conditionMessage`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/conditions.html)`(``w``)``, ``"\n"``)`\
`)`\
`# Run of pipeline 'ozone' continued after 1 failed step:`\
`#   'fit': object 'Height' not found`\
`# Steps not run because an input failed: 'coef_table', 'plot', 'summary'`\
`pip`\
`# <pipeflow> ozone (8 steps)`\
`# --------------------------`\
`#          step                   params                            depends  state`\
`# 1:       data                     data                                      done`\
`# 2:       prep                       df                               data   done`\
`# 3: data_table                     data                               prep   done`\
`# 4:        fit                data,xVar                               prep failed`\
`# 5: coef_table                    model                                fit    new`\
`# 6:       plot          model,data,xVar                           fit,prep    new`\
`# 7:    summary                    model                                fit    new`\
`# 8:     report table,coefs,plot,summary data_table,coef_table,plot,summary   done`\
`#                    out`\
`# 1: <data.frame[153x6]>`\
`# 2: <data.frame[153x7]>`\
`# 3:     <huxtable[6x7]>`\
`# 4: <error/simpleError>`\
`# 5:              [NULL]`\
`# 6:              [NULL]`\
`# 7:              [NULL]`\
`# 8:        <pub_doc[2]>`\
`# --------------------------`\
`# <continued> last run: 2026-11-06 15:00:18 (0.055 s)`\
`# steps: 4 done, 1 failed, 3 new`

The run warns (class `pipeflow_run_failed`), but the document is there.
The steps `coef_table`, `plot` and `summary` didn’t run either, and each
shows as an error box that names the cause:

\
`doc`` ``<-`` ``pip``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]`\
[`show`](https://rdrr.io/r/methods/show.html)`(``doc``)`

A Shiny app can show such a document while the user fixes a param. The
viewer
([`pub_viewer_server()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_viewer_ui.md))
only renders the document that its `doc` reactive returns; it never runs
a pipeline. The app does that: it calls `pip_run(on_error = "continue")`
and passes the output of the layout step. A few rules go with it:

- Write `~try()` for **every** input of a layout step that may arrive
  failed. If you forget it for one input, pipeflow skips the layout step
  after a failure of that input, and there is no document at all.
- Computation steps choose `~try()` per argument, as in any pipeline.
  Normally they take a plain `~step`, so they never see a failure
  object.
- A report file is different:
  [`pub_render()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)
  refuses a document with error items, so that a report with a hole in
  it is never published by accident. (The report spec of
  [`pub_report_spec()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_report_spec.md)
  can allow them.) Run the pipeline of a report with the default
  `on_error = "stop"`; the failed step then stops the run and there is
  no document.

\
[`pub_render`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)`(``doc``, ``"docx"``)`\
`# ``Error```  in `pub_render()`: ``\
`# ``!`` Can't render a document with error items (failed steps):`\
`# ``✖`` step 'fit' failed: object 'Height' not found`\
`# ``✖`` step 'fit' failed: object 'Height' not found`\
`# ``✖`` step 'fit' failed: object 'Height' not found`\
`# ``ℹ```  Reports run the pipeline with `on_error = "stop"`; error items are for the viewer. ``

Set the param back and the next run repairs the steps that failed:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Temp.Celsius"``)``)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`pip`\
`# <pipeflow> ozone (8 steps)`\
`# --------------------------`\
`#          step                   params                            depends state`\
`# 1:       data                     data                                     done`\
`# 2:       prep                       df                               data  done`\
`# 3: data_table                     data                               prep  done`\
`# 4:        fit                data,xVar                               prep  done`\
`# 5: coef_table                    model                                fit  done`\
`# 6:       plot          model,data,xVar                           fit,prep  done`\
`# 7:    summary                    model                                fit  done`\
`# 8:     report table,coefs,plot,summary data_table,coef_table,plot,summary  done`\
`#                                            out`\
`# 1:                         <data.frame[153x6]>`\
`# 2:                         <data.frame[153x7]>`\
`# 3:                             <huxtable[6x7]>`\

### Select the steps of a report by tags

A pipeline often has more outputs than one report shows. Tag the steps
with pipeflow’s tags, then let the tags decide which steps a layout step
uses.
[`pub_layout_inputs()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_layout_inputs.md)
returns the `~try(step)` references of a pipeline or of a view on it,
for a layout step whose function takes `...`:

\
`tagged`` ``<-`` `[`pip_reset`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_reset.html)`(`[`pip_clone`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_clone.html)`(``pip``)``)`\
[`pip_tag`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_tag.html)`(`[`pip_view`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_view.html)`(``tagged``, step ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"summary"``, ``"coef_table"``)``)``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"short"``, ``"long"``)``)`\
[`pip_tag`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_tag.html)`(`[`pip_view`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_view.html)`(``tagged``, step ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"data_table"``, ``"plot"``)``)``, ``"long"``)`

Each report is a layout step with its own tag. Add them last, because
the steps are read when
[`pub_layout_inputs()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_layout_inputs.md)
is called:

\
`tagged`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(`\
`        ``"short"``,`\
`        \``(``...``)`` `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(`[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``...``)``, title ``=`` ``"Short report"``)``,`\
`        params ``=`` `[`pub_layout_inputs`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_layout_inputs.md)`(`[`pip_view`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_view.html)`(``tagged``, tags ``=`` ``"short"``)``)`\
`    ``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(`\
`        ``"long"``,`\
`        \``(``...``)`` `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(`[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``...``)``, title ``=`` ``"Long report"``)``,`\
`        params ``=`` `[`pub_layout_inputs`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_layout_inputs.md)`(`[`pip_view`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_view.html)`(``tagged``, tags ``=`` ``"long"``)``)`\
`    ``)`

`list(...)` is a named list, which becomes one section per step, titled
by the step’s name. `unname(list(...))` places the outputs one after the
other, without sections. The reports share the steps, and a run of a
view computes just what its report needs:

\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(`[`pip_view`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_view.html)`(``tagged``, step ``=`` ``"short"``)``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`tagged`\
`# <pipeflow> ozone (10 steps)`\
`# ---------------------------`\
`#           step                             params                            depends state`\
`#  1:       data                               data                                     done`\
`#  2:       prep                                 df                               data  done`\
`#  3: data_table                               data                               prep   new`\
`#  4:        fit                          data,xVar                               prep  done`\
`#  5: coef_table                              model                                fit  done`\
`#  6:       plot                    model,data,xVar                           fit,prep   new`\
`#  7:    summary                              model                                fit  done`\
`#  8:     report           table,coefs,plot,summary data_table,coef_table,plot,summary   new`\
`#  9:      short                 coef_table,summary                 coef_table,summary  done`\
`# 10:       long data_table,coef_table,plot,summary data_table,coef_table,plot,summary   new`\
`#                                             out       tags`\
`#  1:                         <data.frame[153x6]>           `\
`#  2:                         <data.frame[153x7]>           `\
`#  3:                                      [NULL]       long`\
`#  4:                                    <lm[13]>           `\
`#  5:                             <huxtable[3x4]> short,long`\
`#  6:                                      [NULL]       long`\
`#  7: The model explains **49%** of the varian... short,long`\
`#  8:                                      [NULL]           `\
`#  9:                                <pub_doc[2]>           `\
`# 10:                                      [NULL]           `\
`# ---------------------------`\
`# <ready> last run: 2026-11-06 15:00:19 (0.026 s)`\
`# steps: 6 done, 4 new`\
[`show`](https://rdrr.io/r/methods/show.html)`(``tagged``[[``"short"``, ``"out"``]``]``)`

## Short report

- [1 coef_table](#pubflow-sec-1)

### 1 coef_table

| Term         | Estimate |   Lower |   Upper |
|--------------|---------:|--------:|--------:|
| (Intercept)  |  -69.277 | -90.906 | -47.648 |
| Temp.Celsius |    4.372 |   3.540 |   5.203 |

### 2 summary

The model explains **49%** of the variance of the ozone concentration.

The steps `plot` and `data_table` are only needed by the long report and
did not run.

Tags are one way to select; every view works, e.g. one on the steps that
directly depend on `fit`:
`pub_layout_inputs(pip_view(tagged, depends = "fit"))`. (A view that
contains partitioned steps, see below, and other steps needs
`exec = "reduce"` for the layout step; otherwise the layout step runs
once per partition.)

### Layouts that change with the data

The structure of a document often depends on the data: one section per
batch, per site, per month. Choose among three ways, from the simplest.

#### A step that returns a named list

The step `monthly` returns one table for every month in the data. A
named list becomes one section per name when it is placed in a document,
so the layout step needs no code for the months. If the data change, the
sections change with them:

\
`monthly_tables`` ``<-`` ``function``(``data``)`` ``{`\
`    ``months`` ``<-`` `[`split`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/split.html)`(``data``, ``data``$``Month``)`\
`    `[`names`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/names.html)`(``months``)`` ``<-`` ``month.name``[`[`as.integer`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/integer.html)`(`[`names`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/names.html)`(``months``)``)``]`\
`    `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``months``, \``(``d``)`` ``{`\
`        `[`pub_table`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_table.md)`(`\
`            `[`data.frame`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html)`(`\
`                Variable ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"Ozone (ppb)"``, ``"Temperature (°C)"``)``,`\
`                Mean ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(`[`mean`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/mean.html)`(``d``$``Ozone``, na.rm ``=`` ``TRUE``)``, `[`mean`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/mean.html)`(``d``$``Temp.Celsius``)``)`\
`            ``)``,`\
`            caption ``=`` `[`sprintf`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/sprintf.html)`(``"Means in %s"``, ``month.name``[``d``$``Month``[[``1L``]``]``]``)``,`\
`            digits ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``Mean ``=`` ``1L``)`\
`        ``)`\
`    ``}``)`\
`}`\
\
`p2`` ``<-`` `[`pip_clone`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_clone.html)`(``pip``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"monthly"``, ``monthly_tables``, params ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``data ``=`` ``~``prep``)``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"by_month"``, ``function``(``tables`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``monthly``)``)`` ``{`\
`        `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``tables``, title ``=`` ``"Means by month"``)`\
`    ``}``)`\
\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``p2``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`

This is the right tool when the content of a section is a few outputs
made in one step. A step that returns a list is one step: if it fails,
all sections fail together, and the pipeline can’t cache or re-run a
single section.

#### Split steps: one partition per batch

If each batch needs its own chain of steps (a fit, a table and a figure
per batch), use pipeflow’s split steps: a step with `exec = "split"`
returns a list, and every step downstream runs once per element, the
*partitions*, until a step with `exec = "reduce"` takes them all. A
layout step downstream of a split step runs once per partition and
returns the section of that partition. The step doesn’t get the key of
its partition, so the title comes from the data:

\
`ps`` ``<-`` `[`pip_new`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_new.html)`(``"by-month"``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"data"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``airquality``)`` ``{`\
`        ``data``$``Temp.Celsius`` ``<-`` ``(``data``$``Temp`` ``-`` ``32``)`` ``*`` ``5`` ``/`` ``9`\
`        ``data`\
`    ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(`\
`        ``"months"``,`\
`        ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``~``data``)`` `[`split`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/split.html)`(``data``, ``data``$``Month``)``,`\
`        exec ``=`` ``"split"`\
`    ``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"fit"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``~``months``)`` `[`lm`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html)`(``Ozone`` ``~`` ``Temp.Celsius``, data ``=`` ``data``)``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"table"``, ``coef_table``, params ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``model ``=`` ``~``fit``)``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"plot"``, ``function``(``model`` ``=`` ``~``fit``, ``data`` ``=`` ``~``months``)`` ``{`\
`        ``fit_figure``(``model``, ``data``, ``"Temp.Celsius"``)`\
`    ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"section"``, ``function``(`\
`        ``data`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``months``)``,`\
`        ``table`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``table``)``,`\
`        ``plot`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``plot``)`\
`    ``)`` ``{`\
`        `[`pub_section`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``month.name``[``data``$``Month``[[``1L``]``]``]``, ``table``, ``plot``)`\
`    ``}``)`

A last step with `exec = "reduce"` gets the sections of all partitions
as one partitioned output and builds the document.
[`unname()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/unname.html) places the sections one
after the other; without it each partition becomes a sub-section titled
by its key, around the section the step returned:

\
`ps`` ``<-`` `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(`\
`    ``ps``,`\
`    ``"doc"``,`\
`    ``function``(``sections`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``section``)``)`` ``{`\
`        `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(`\
`            `[`pub_section`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``"Months"``, `[`unname`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/unname.html)`(``sections``)``)``,`\
`            title ``=`` ``"Ozone by month"`\
`        ``)`\
`    ``}``,`\
`    exec ``=`` ``"reduce"`\
`)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``ps``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\

Pipeflow’s split steps fail per partition. If the table of one month
fails, its section shows an error box and the other months are complete.
A failed batch is also the only one that runs again in the next run, as
long as the failed step’s params, exec mode and inputs are unchanged, no
input ran again and the run is not forced. Note that a param change
outdates a whole step: all its partitions run again, not only some.

Choose between the two like this: the named list is easiest if the
content of a section is made in one step. Split steps pay off when the
chain per batch is long, when it can fail, or when its results are
expensive to recompute after a failure. A third way, *nested pipelines*
(a pipeline that is a step function through
[`as.function()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.function.html)), is for
batches that share one param set but are computed by a pipeline of their
own; see pipeflow’s vignette [Nested
pipelines](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pipeflow/vignettes/v05b-nested-pipeline.html).

#### What does not work: add steps while running

A step that adds steps to the pipeline in the course of a run (a step
function that calls `pip_add(.self, ...)` for every batch it finds) does
not work for documents: the layout step can’t name a step that does not
exist when it is added, because
[`pip_add()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)
rejects unknown `~step` references, and
[`pub_layout_inputs()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_layout_inputs.md)
lists the steps present at that moment. Use a named list or a split step
instead; both have as many outputs as there are batches.

\
[`pip_new`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_new.html)`(``"tmp"``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"report"``, ``function``(``table`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``batch_a_table``)``)`` `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``table``)``)`\
`# ``Error``:`\
`# ``!`` while adding step 'report' - cannot reference unknown steps: 'batch_a_table'`

### Documents across pipelines

Groups that have their own params, their own inputs or their own runs
are better as *independent pipelines* made by one constructor than as
one pipeline with partitions. A study can have one pipeline per test
(assay, water content, …), each with its own specification limits, its
own parameter tab and its own run, possibly in a parallel worker. The
report puts the parts together.

A constructor for a group’s pipeline. The layout step `content` makes
the part of the report for this group. It takes a plain `~table`, so it
is skipped when the table fails: the failure is handled where the parts
are collected:

\
`month_pipeline`` ``<-`` ``function``(``name``, ``month``)`` ``{`\
`    `[`pip_new`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_new.html)`(``name``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"data"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``airquality``, ``month`` ``=`` ``5L``)`` ``{`\
`            ``data``[``data``$``Month`` ``==`` ``month``, ``]`\
`        ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"mean"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``~``data``, ``limit`` ``=`` ``40``)`` ``{`\
`            ``m`` ``<-`` `[`mean`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/mean.html)`(``data``$``Ozone``, na.rm ``=`` ``TRUE``)`\
`            ``if`` ``(`[`is.nan`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/is.finite.html)`(``m``)``)`` `[`stop`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/stop.html)`(``"no ozone values"``)`\
`            `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``mean ``=`` ``m``, limit ``=`` ``limit``)`\
`        ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"table"``, ``function``(``res`` ``=`` ``~``mean``)`` ``{`\
`            `[`pub_table`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_table.md)`(`\
`                `[`data.frame`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/data.frame.html)`(`\
`                    Quantity ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"Mean ozone"``, ``"Limit"``)``,`\
`                    Value ``=`` `[`unname`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/unname.html)`(``res``)`\
`                ``)``,`\
`                caption ``=`` ``"Ozone (ppb)"``,`\
`                digits ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``Value ``=`` ``1L``)`\
`            ``)`\
`        ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"content"``, ``function``(``table`` ``=`` ``~``table``)`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``table``)``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(`[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``month ``=`` ``month``)``)`\
`}`\
\
`pips`` ``<-`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(`\
`    May ``=`` ``month_pipeline``(``"May"``, ``5L``)``,`\
`    June ``=`` ``month_pipeline``(``"June"``, ``6L``)``,`\
`    July ``=`` ``month_pipeline``(``"July"``, ``7L``)`\
`)`

Each group is run on its own. Here a loop runs them; an app can run each
in a parallel worker, which does the same and returns the pipeline:

\
`for`` ``(``p`` ``in`` ``pips``)`` ``{`\
`    `[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``p``, on_error ``=`` ``"continue"``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`}`\
`pips``$``May`\
`# <pipeflow> May (4 steps)`\
`# ------------------------`\
`#       step     params depends state                out`\
`# 1:    data data,month          done <data.frame[31x6]>`\
`# 2:    mean data,limit    data  done  23.61538,40.00000`\
`# 3:   table        res    mean  done    <huxtable[3x2]>`\
`# 4: content      table   table  done          <list[1]>`\
`# ------------------------`\
`# <ready> last run: 2026-11-06 15:00:20 (0.011 s)`\
`# steps: 4 done`

#### Read the parts with `pub_out()`

The report takes the output of a group’s layout step with
[`pub_out()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_out.md). It
differs from `p[["content", "out"]]` in one respect: it returns the
output only if the step is `done`. After a failed run a step keeps its
*earlier* output, so `p[[step, "out"]]` could silently put old results
into a report.

\
[`pub_out`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_out.md)`(``pips``$``May``, ``"content"``)`\
`# [[1]]`\
`#                                             Ozone (ppb)                                             `\
`#                                      ──────────────────────────`\
`#                                        ``Quantity  ``   ``    Value``  `\
`#                                      ──────────────────────────`\
`#                                        Mean ozone        23.6  `\
`#                                        Limit             40.0  `\
`#                                      ──────────────────────────`\
`# `\
`# Column names: Quantity, Value`

If the step is not done,
[`pub_out()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_out.md)
signals an error that names the pipeline and the failed steps. With
`on_error = "item"` it returns an error item instead, which a document
shows as an error box:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pips``$``June``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``month ``=`` ``13L``)``)`\
[`suppressWarnings`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/warning.html)`(`[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pips``$``June``, on_error ``=`` ``"continue"``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)``)`\
\
[`pub_out`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_out.md)`(``pips``$``June``, ``"content"``)`\
`# ``Error```  in `pub_out()`: ``\
`# ``!`` The output of step 'content' of pipeline 'June' is not up to date (state "outdated").`\
`# ``✖`` Step 'mean' failed: no ozone values`

#### A report pipeline

A **report pipeline** puts the parts together. Its input step receives
the parts as a param value, a layout step builds the document, and the
rest of the report (cross-group tables, a summary of all groups) are
ordinary steps of this pipeline. pipeflow skips a param value that is
[`identical()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/identical.html) to the old one,
so parts that did not change don’t outdate anything:

\
`report`` ``<-`` `[`pip_new`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_new.html)`(``"report"``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"parts"``, ``function``(``parts`` ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``)``)`` ``parts``)`` ``|>`\
`    `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"doc"``, ``function``(``parts`` ``=`` ``~`` `[`try`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/try.html)`(``parts``)``)`` ``{`\
`        `[`pub_doc`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(`[`pub_section`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_doc.md)`(``"Ozone by month"``, ``parts``)``, title ``=`` ``"Study report"``)`\
`    ``}``)`

The parts are a named list, so each group becomes a section titled by
its name. A group whose pipeline failed is shown as an error box in its
section, and the other groups’ results are in the document:

\
`parts`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``pips``, ``pub_out``, step ``=`` ``"content"``, on_error ``=`` ``"item"``)`\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``report``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``parts ``=`` ``parts``)``)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``report``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
[`show`](https://rdrr.io/r/methods/show.html)`(``report``[[``"doc"``, ``"out"``]``]``)`

Repair the group and run the report pipeline again. The group’s own run
re-runs only the steps that the param outdated, and the report pipeline
gets the new part:

\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pips``$``June``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``month ``=`` ``6L``)``)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pips``$``June``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`parts`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``pips``, ``pub_out``, step ``=`` ``"content"``, on_error ``=`` ``"item"``)`\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``report``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``parts ``=`` ``parts``)``)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``report``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`report`\
`# <pipeflow> report (2 steps)`\
`# ---------------------------`\
`#     step params depends state          out`\
`# 1: parts  parts          done    <list[3]>`\
`# 2:   doc  parts   parts  done <pub_doc[2]>`\
`# ---------------------------`\
`# <ready> last run: 2026-11-06 15:00:20 (0.004 s)`\
`# steps: 2 done`

Two things to know when a worker runs the group’s pipeline:

- A pipeline survives
  [`saveRDS()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/readRDS.html), so a worker
  returns the *run pipeline* and the app keeps all states: the next run
  of that pipeline re-runs only outdated steps. The returned pipeline
  holds copies of its outputs, in which ggplots get new cache keys, so
  make figures in such steps with `pub_figure(render = TRUE)`: the step
  then returns the picture, not the plot.
- Computations across groups (e.g. a table of all minima) are steps of
  the report pipeline. Give them the groups’ data as parts read with
  [`pub_out()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_out.md),
  too.

### Test layout steps

A layout step is a function, and it is easy to test, with two kinds of
tests. Both work on small data, so they run fast.

**The structure.** A layout step references the steps by their names,
and
[`pip_add()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)
already rejects a name that does not exist (see above). Run the pipeline
on a small data set and check the document:

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`testthat`](https://testthat.r-lib.org)`)`\
\
[`test_that`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_that.html)`(``"the report has the sections and a figure"``, ``{`\
`    ``pip`` ``<-`` ``report_pipeline``(``)`` ``# your constructor`\
`    `[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``data ``=`` ``airquality``[``1``:``30``, ``]``)``)`\
`    `[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
\
`    ``doc`` ``<-`` ``pip``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]`\
`    `[`expect_s3_class`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/inheritance-expectations.html)`(``doc``, ``"pub_doc"``)`\
`    `[`expect_match`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/expect_match.html)`(`[`as.character`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html)`(`[`pub_html`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_html.md)`(``doc``)``)``, ``"Coefficients with 95%"``)`\
`}``)`

**The failures.** A forgotten `~try()` is not an error: it makes the
layout step skip, so the viewer shows no document after a failure. Make
a step fail with a bad param, run on `on_error = "continue"`, and check
that the document is still there and reports the failure:

\
`broken`` ``<-`` `[`pip_clone`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_clone.html)`(``pip``)`\
[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``broken``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Height"``)``)`\
[`suppressWarnings`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/warning.html)`(`[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``broken``, on_error ``=`` ``"continue"``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)``)`\
\
`doc`` ``<-`` ``broken``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]`\
[`class`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/class.html)`(``doc``)`\
`# [1] "pub_doc"  "pub_node"`\
[`grepl`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/grep.html)`(``"Step 'fit' failed"``, `[`as.character`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html)`(`[`pub_html`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_html.md)`(``doc``)``)``, fixed ``=`` ``TRUE``)`\
`# [1] TRUE`

As a test:

\
[`test_that`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_that.html)`(``"the report survives a failed fit"``, ``{`\
`    ``pip`` ``<-`` ``report_pipeline``(``)`\
`    `[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Height"``)``)`\
`    `[`suppressWarnings`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/warning.html)`(`[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, on_error ``=`` ``"continue"``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)``)`\
\
`    ``doc`` ``<-`` ``pip``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]`\
`    `[`expect_s3_class`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/inheritance-expectations.html)`(``doc``, ``"pub_doc"``)`\
`    `[`expect_match`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/expect_match.html)`(`[`as.character`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html)`(`[`pub_html`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_html.md)`(``doc``)``)``, ``"Step 'fit' failed"``, fixed ``=`` ``TRUE``)`\
`}``)`

For a report that must never be published with a hole in it, test the
other direction: the run with the default `on_error = "stop"` stops, and
[`pub_render()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)
refuses a document with error items:

\
[`test_that`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_that.html)`(``"a failed step stops the report run"``, ``{`\
`    ``pip`` ``<-`` ``report_pipeline``(``)`\
`    `[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Height"``)``)`\
`    `[`expect_error`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/expect_error.html)`(`[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)``, class ``=`` ``"pipeflow_step_error"``)`\
`}``)`\
\
[`test_that`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/test_that.html)`(``"pub_render() refuses error items"``, ``{`\
`    ``pip`` ``<-`` ``report_pipeline``(``)`\
`    `[`pip_set_params`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_set_params.html)`(``pip``, `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``xVar ``=`` ``"Height"``)``)`\
`    `[`suppressWarnings`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/warning.html)`(`[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``pip``, on_error ``=`` ``"continue"``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)``)`\
\
`    `[`expect_error`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/reference/expect_error.html)`(`\
`        `[`pub_render`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_render.md)`(``pip``[[``"report"``, ``"out"``]``]``, ``"docx"``)``,`\
`        class ``=`` ``"pubflow_render_error"`\
`    ``)`\
`}``)`

### Steps that make figures

A ggplot keeps the environment in which it was made: the
[`aes()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html) mappings are
quosures that point to the frame of the step, and that frame points to
where the step function was defined. If that is a pipeline constructor,
a figure carries the pipeline and everything the constructor holds,
e.g. the data. As long as the figure stays in the pipeline, nobody
notices. It costs as soon as it travels or lives without its pipeline: a
document sent to a worker, saved with
[`saveRDS()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/readRDS.html) or kept by a viewer.

pubflow doesn’t check this at run time; the remedy is a habit:

- Write steps that make figures, fits or closures as **top-level
  functions** (in your package or script). Given to
  [`pip_add()`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)
  directly (with `params` for the `~step` references, as for
  `coef_table`), neither the figure nor the stored step function
  encloses the constructor. An inline wrapper that only calls a
  top-level helper, as `plot` above, keeps the *figure* free of the
  constructor, but pipeflow stores the wrapper as given, so the saved
  pipeline still holds the constructor’s frame.
- Keep step functions out of a function that also holds large data. If a
  constructor takes the data as an argument, steps defined inside it
  enclose that data.
- Let an app test the serialized size of its real documents. The example
  makes the cost visible: a constructor holds 16 MB of data (`big`, used
  by another step) that the figure doesn’t show. The same figure is made
  by a function written inline in the constructor and by the top-level
  `small_plot()`:

\
`small_plot`` ``<-`` ``function``(``data``)`` ``{`\
`    `[`pub_figure`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_figure.md)`(`\
`        `[`ggplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggplot.html)`(``data``, `[`aes`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html)`(``.data``$``Temp``, ``.data``$``Ozone``)``)`` ``+`` `[`geom_point`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_point.html)`(``na.rm ``=`` ``TRUE``)``,`\
`        caption ``=`` ``"Ozone by temperature"`\
`    ``)`\
`}`\
\
`make_pipeline`` ``<-`` ``function``(``big``)`` ``{`\
`    `[`pip_new`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_new.html)`(``"sizes"``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"data"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``airquality``)`` ``data``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"other"``, ``function``(``x`` ``=`` ``big``)`` `[`mean`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/mean.html)`(``x``)``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"inline"``, ``function``(``data`` ``=`` ``~``data``)`` ``{`\
`            `[`pub_figure`](https://rpahl.github.io/pubflow/reference/pub_figure.md)`(`\
`                `[`ggplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggplot.html)`(``data``, `[`aes`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html)`(``.data``$``Temp``, ``.data``$``Ozone``)``)`` ``+`\
`                    `[`geom_point`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_point.html)`(``na.rm ``=`` ``TRUE``)``,`\
`                caption ``=`` ``"Ozone by temperature"`\
`            ``)`\
`        ``}``)`` ``|>`\
`        `[`pip_add`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_add.html)`(``"top_level"``, ``small_plot``, params ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``data ``=`` ``~``data``)``)`\
`}`\
\
`sizes`` ``<-`` ``make_pipeline``(``big ``=`` `[`rnorm`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Normal.html)`(``2e6``)``)`\
[`pip_run`](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/reference/pip_run.html)`(``sizes``, lgr ``=`` ``NULL``)`\
`figures`` ``<-`` ``sizes``[[``"out"``]``]``[`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"inline"``, ``"top_level"``)``]`\
[`round`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Round.html)`(`[`vapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``figures``, \``(``f``)`` `[`length`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/length.html)`(`[`serialize`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/serialize.html)`(``f``, ``NULL``)``)`` ``/`` ``1e6``, `[`numeric`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/numeric.html)`(``1L``)``)``, ``2``)`` ``# MB`\
`#    inline top_level `\
`#     16.79      0.79`
